rows: A reconciliation you completed
Describe what did not match, how you traced it and what changed.
It is the daily work of audit and accounting teams.
A tax computation you explained to a layperson
Say who it was for and what they did differently afterwards.
Advice that changes a decision is what clients pay for.
Practical-training work you can discuss without breaking confidentiality
Describe the type of engagement and your role, never client names.
Firms check that you understand confidentiality as much as the work.
A spreadsheet model or dashboard
Show how you built it and what it flagged.
Reporting and finance roles value people who can make numbers visible.
Your own exam plan
State how you schedule revision around work.
It shows the stamina interviewers worry about.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Weak lines in a CA interview, and what to say instead
rows: I Like Numbers.
It Is Too General to Remember.
Give One Task with Numbers That You Enjoyed and Why.
I Like Numbers.
It Is Too General to Remember.
Give One Task with Numbers That You Enjoyed and Why.
My parents wanted me to do CA.
It sounds like the choice is not yours and invites doubt about your motivation.
Say what you saw about the work that you wanted to try, even if family first suggested it.
CA gives security and good pay.
Every candidate says it, and it suggests you will leave for a better offer.
Describe the work you want to do and what you will learn in this role.
I will start my own practice soon.
A firm may fear you will leave before you are useful.
Say you want to build depth first and may open a practice after real experience.

Round 1: your story
Write your three moments with numbers or rules.
A stranger can repeat your story back accurately after one hearing. Field check: each has a task, a result and a lesson.
Round 2: delivery
Say your answer aloud and time it.
You finish in about a minute and it sounds like you, not a script. Field check: under a minute, no jargon.
Round 3: the hard question
Add the audit, tax or finance lane and the reason.
Your answer to the question you fear holds up without notes. Field check: a listener can repeat it back.
Round 4: full mock
Run a mock with a senior or friend using the five follow-ups.
You keep the same facts when a follow-up changes the angle. Field check: you stay calm on the attempts question.
